results.claim: Cassaigne's first-difference method (Complexity and special factors, Bull. SMF 125 (1997) 1-26, Zbl 0921.68065) gives p(L+1)-p(L) = sum_{f in F(L)}(d+(f)-1) for an extendable language with d+ >= 1, so HANDOFF 3.4's form p(L+1)-p(L) = #right-special is correct only there; the right-special/extendability framework is as in Cassaigne-Nicolas, arXiv:0903.1627.
results.paper_quote: 0903.1627v5 Def. 1: 'We say that a word w in A* is a (right-)special factor of the language L if there exist a, b in A with a != b such that both wa and wb are factors of L.' Def. 2: 'We say that the language L is (right-)extendable if for each w in L, there exists a in A such that wa in L.' The identity is in the work the Status names: Cassaigne, 'Complexite et facteurs speciaux' (Zbl 0921.68065), Prop. 3.4 (OCR): 'Soit L un langage factoriel prolongeable. Alors sum_{u in L inter A^n} m_d(u) = sum m_g(u) = p(n+1) - p(n)', with m_d(u) = #{x in A^k : ux in L} - 1 = d+(u) - 1.
results.doc_quote: Cassaigne's first-difference method (Complexity and special factors, Bull. SMF 125 (1997) 1-26, Zbl 0921.68065) gives p(L+1)-p(L)=sum_{f in F(L)}(d+(f)-1) for an *extendable* language, where d+>=1, so HANDOFF 3.4's form p(L+1)-p(L)=#right-special is correct only there; right-special/extendability as in [Cassaigne-Nicolas, arXiv:0903.1627].
results.notes: Read 0903.1627v5 HTML + v5 LaTeX source: it defines right-special (Def. 1) and extendable (Def. 2) exactly as used, but has no equality; its closing section-3 exercise (Ex. 8, v5) gives only p(n+1)-p(n) <= (alpha-1)s(n), and >= s(n) if L is extendable. The equality is Prop. 3.4 of the paper the Status names: Zbl 0921.68065 = Bull. Belg. Math. Soc. Simon Stevin 4 (1997) 67-88, not Bull. SMF 125 (1997) 1-26. Caveats: the paper needs L factorial and prolongeable, the doc only extendable; the unweighted #right-special form is Prop. 3.1, stated 'alphabet binaire', and order >1 factors count with multiplicity, so #RS = sum(d+-1) needs d+ <= 2. Source read via OCR of the EMIS/Wayback scan.
